questions.q: Why does averaging many trees usually beat a single deep tree?
options: Each tree is individually more accurate
Averaging cuts variance, because the trees' errors point in different directions
It removes the need for training data
It makes the model easier to draw as a diagram
questions.explain: A deep tree has high variance. Combining many different trees averages out their individual errors, reducing variance without raising bias much.

questions.q: Which two sources of randomness does a random forest use to make its trees different?
options: Random labels and random learning rates
Shuffled columns and deleted rows
Bootstrap samples of rows, and a random subset of features considered at each split
Random test sets and random scalers
questions.explain: Each tree is trained on a bootstrap sample of the rows, and each split considers only a random subset of the features. Both keep the trees from making identical mistakes.

options: The training accuracy
A validation estimate made by predicting each row using only trees that did not train on it
The accuracy on a manually held-out test set
The number of trees that failed to converge
questions.explain: Because each tree leaves out about a third of the rows, each row can be scored by the trees that never saw it, giving a free validation estimate.

questions.q: In the lesson's sweep, cross-validated accuracy rose quickly from 1 to about 5 trees and then leveled off near 0.96. What is the practical takeaway?
options: Adding more trees causes overfitting
One tree is always enough
Accuracy must decrease after 5 trees
More trees reduce variance with diminishing returns, so extra trees mostly add training time
questions.explain: Forest performance improves and then plateaus. More trees don't overfit on their own, but beyond the plateau they cost time and memory for little gain.

questions.q: What is a real drawback of a random forest compared with a single decision tree?
options: It needs features to be scaled
It cannot handle non-linear relationships
It overfits more than a single tree always does
You lose the simple readable path of one tree, and it is slower and larger
questions.explain: A hundred trees can't be read as one checklist, and they take more time and memory. Forests handle non-linearity well and need no scaling.
